title: Convention Center Pickup: Confirm the Building and Exit
description: Leaving a convention for your hotel or airport? Confirm the building, passenger exit, loading location and ready time before arranging the pickup.
cta: Give your convention pickup a precise meeting point.
image_alt: A rolling work bag and folded umbrella beside glass entrance doors and a rain-wet city sidewalk.
body:
For a convention-center pickup, give the ride provider the exact building, the passenger exit you will use and a loading location it has agreed to serve. Add a reachable traveler contact and the time you expect to be ready outside. The venue name, a hotel name or a map pin alone may not identify the right meeting point.

Large events can span several buildings and finish at more than one door. Treat the event's attendee entrance, your eventual exit and the vehicle's permitted loading place as three details to confirm, rather than assuming they are interchangeable.

Start with the event building

Check your organizer's current registration instructions, session location and venue map. Record the building name as well as its street address. If the final meeting is in another building, plan the return pickup from that location instead of automatically reusing the morning drop-off.

Moscone Center provides a useful San Francisco example. Its official directions page identifies Moscone West at 800 Howard Street, at Fourth and Howard. It separately lists the administrative office at 747 Howard Street. That office listing is not a substitute for your event's attendee instructions or an agreed passenger pickup point.

Send the actual attendee location to the provider and ask it to confirm the practical loading arrangement for your date. Do not label a loading dock as a passenger entrance just because it appears on a venue map. Moscone's loading-dock guidance concerns freight operations coordinated with the event's General Service Contractor; it does not establish a passenger meeting place.

Turn the exit into a meeting point

Before the event ends, confirm these details with the organizer and ride provider:

  • Building and exit: the name on the event map and the door or lobby you will leave through.
  • Street-level location: the agreed loading address or clearly described meeting point, including the street side when relevant.
  • Access needs: a suitable route from the meeting room to that location, confirmed with the venue if assistance or step-free access is needed.
  • Readiness: time to leave the session, collect belongings and reach the meeting point before loading.
  • Contact and fallback: who will answer the provider, and how a changed meeting point will be acknowledged.

A landmark can help identify a door, but it does not confirm that a vehicle may wait there. Follow current event traffic instructions and the provider's acknowledged loading plan. If you cannot find the vehicle, reconnect before crossing to another street or walking around the campus.

Separate session end from pickup readiness

A session ending at 5 p.m. is not the same as being ready to load at 5 p.m. Badge checkout, a coat check, a hotel bag collection or a walk from another building may still be ahead. Work backward from any onward commitment and agree on a pickup time that includes your actual exit tasks. There is no universal convention-exit buffer.

Illustrative plan: a traveler attends a final session in one building, collects a work bag there and then needs a suitcase held at the hotel. The quote should identify the hotel collection as a separate stop, including who retrieves the suitcase. It should not describe only a direct convention-to-airport ride. Confirm the hotel handoff and provider's stop arrangement before relying on either.

If the session runs late, use the contact on the existing reservation. State whether you are still in the meeting, walking to the exit or ready at the agreed point. Ask the provider to confirm the revised plan and any applicable waiting or change terms; sending a message does not itself confirm a change.

Give one person the group check

For colleagues leaving together, nominate one contact to confirm that everyone and their bags are present. Share the actual passenger and luggage count with the provider. A conference registration count does not establish the number of riders or the space needed in a vehicle.

If someone leaves for dinner while others go to the airport, identify the separate destinations before the pickup. Use our multiple-stop planning guide to organize the request. Equipment that needs a freight or receiving arrangement belongs in a separate presentation-equipment handoff.

Send one copyable pickup brief

Convention pickup brief
Event and date: [event / full local date]. Building: [name and attendee address]. Exit: [door/lobby]. Please confirm the passenger loading point and access instructions. We expect to be ready at [time], after [bag collection or other task]. Riders and luggage: [details]. Destination and intermediate stop: [details]. Traveler contact: [number/channel]. If the exit changes, please acknowledge the new meeting point before we move.

For an existing Koast reservation, use your confirmation or agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment of changes. A new quote does not amend that ride. For a new event journey, explore Koast corporate transportation and include the confirmed building, exit tasks, passengers and onward destination in your quote request.
